records.name: PURR (Philadelphia Urgent Rescue and Relief)
records.summary: An all-volunteer cat rescue run on donations. It trims colonies of outdoor cats, takes in sick or unwanted cats, runs a sanctuary, and places cats through adoption and foster homes.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer with sanctuary care, trap-neuter-return work, or driving cats where they need to go. You can also foster a cat, or help at the PURR Cat Cafe in Bridesburg, where adoptable cats live while they wait for homes.

schedule.text: No regular volunteer meeting schedule is published. The PURR Cat Cafe is open noon to 6 pm on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and Mondays. Tuesday to Thursday hours are not listed.

cost.text: Volunteering and fostering are unpaid. Cat cafe visits cost $15 for regular admission, $10 all day on Fridays, and half price on Mondays.

first_step.how: Join PURR's volunteer Facebook group to see the open roles, or fill in the PURR Volunteer Form, a Google form linked from the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page names two clear ways to start, says people of all skill and physical levels can help, and says the group always needs more volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer jobs range from sanctuary care, such as cleaning, replacing supplies, trimming shrubs and playing with the cats, to trap-neuter-return trips and driving cats where they need to go. People of all skill and physical levels can help, according to the site. The volunteer page does not say what training is offered or what shifts look like, so ask in the volunteer Facebook group. Volunteering is unpaid.
first_visit_tips: Book a cafe visit ahead through the booking link on the cafe page. The page does not say whether walk-ins are welcome.
The cafe's front door is at the corner of Orthodox and Thompson Streets.
Street parking can be tight, but the site says spots are usually open near the cemetery on Thompson Street.
The cafe page does not describe wheelchair access or step-free entry, so ask before you visit if you need it.

records.notes: The volunteer page gives no training, minimum age, shift or response-time details. The cafe page gives no accessibility or SEPTA stop details. The Tuesday to Thursday cafe hours are not listed. Cafe admission is charged, so the cost level is low rather than free. The only year on the site is in the copyright footer, which is not used as evidence.
